steps.body: Jumps come in sizes: tens devour distance, ones finish the job. A good plan spends big jumps first and small jumps last.
steps.narration: Jumps come in sizes: tens devour distance, ones finish the job. A good plan spends big jumps first and small jumps last.

widget.prompt: Cover the tens of a 32-journey: three ten-hops from 40.

commonLandings.feedback: Three ones cover 3 of the 32 — the big jumps belong first.

widget.missFeedback: Each hop is 10, going forward. From 40, 3 hops land on 70.
widget.successFeedback: 70 — the tens are spent; two little one-jumps would finish at 72.

predict.prompt: To travel 32 along the line, which plan wins?
predict.reveal: Both arrive, but the mixed plan takes five jumps where ones-only takes thirty-two.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents g2l jump sizes.
invariants: Position on the line IS the number: equal jumps cover equal amounts, and a journey's landing depends only on start, jump size, and direction for g2l jump sizes.
misconceptions: Treating marks as decoration — unequal spacing, jumps of the wrong size, or reading a start mark as a landing.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: Which change — start, jump size, or direction — would move the landing, and which would leave it alone?

widget.prompt: From 40 to 72, which exact plan uses the fewest hops?

options.label: 32 one-jumps, one at a time
options.feedback: That reaches 72, but it takes 32 hops. Tens first make the route much shorter.

options.label: 4 ten-jumps, then turn back
options.feedback: Four ten-jumps reach 80, then eight more one-jumps are needed to return to 72. It is not the fewest-hop route.

options.label: 1 hundred-jump, then walk back
options.feedback: A hundred-jump overshoots far beyond 72, so walking back would add many more hops.

options.label: 3 ten-jumps, then 2 one-jumps
options.feedback: Correct — three tens cover 30 and two ones finish 2: five exact hops total.

steps.body: Finish a mixed-jump route by choosing the small-jump part after the tens are already covered.

widget.prompt: The tens route reached 70. Take two one-hops to finish at 72.

commonLandings.feedback: That makes only one one-hop. Two small hops remain after the tens route reaches 70.

widget.missFeedback: The remaining distance is 2, so use two one-hops from 70 to reach 72.
widget.successFeedback: 72 — big jumps covered the tens; the two small jumps finished exactly.

widget.prompt: After three ten-jumps from 40, which pair of jumps lands exactly on 72?

options.label: 2 ten-jumps to the right
options.feedback: Two more tens would land at 90. Only two ones remain after the tens route.

options.label: 2 one-jumps to the right
options.feedback: Correct — the three tens land at 70, then two one-jumps reach 72.

options.label: 2 one-jumps to the left
options.feedback: Those hops would move from 70 to 68. The landing 72 is to the right of 70.

options.label: 1 ten-jump and 1 one-jump
options.feedback: A ten and a one add 11, so this route would land at 81 instead of 72.
